articles.title: Ohio blogger found guilty of harassment for sending Shrek nude to senator
articles.summary: Ohio political blogger DJ Byrnes was found guilty of harassment after sending a naked Shrek picture to Republican state Sen. Jerry Cirino.
articles.body: A jury found an Ohio political blogger guilty of telecommunications harassment after he sent an explicit image of Shrek to a Republican state senator. On Friday, a judge ordered DJ Byrnes, owner of political commentary blog The Rooster, to pay a $200 fine, according to a report from the Columbus Dispatch. Byrnes texted Ohio Sen. Jerry Cirino in May after he dropped out of the state’s Senate presidential race. As reported by the Columbus Dispatch, Byrnes sent a nude image of Shrek alongside the message: “Good to see you finally made your humiliation public, Young Mussolini! THE PATRIOTS CAUCUS sends its regards!!!!!!!!!!” Cirino filed a police report against Byrnes, “describing his messages as pornographic and harassing,” according to the Columbus Dispatch. Four state police officers arrested Byrnes at the Ohio statehouse in June, the Columbus Dispatch reports. Byrnes was reportedly held in jail overnight even though he posted bail. ”I can’t wait for the jury to see the image that he sent to me,” Cirino said ahead of the trial, according to the Columbus Dispatch. Byrnes pleaded not guilty to telecommunications harassment, claiming that the text was protected free speech. “This wasn’t a free speech issue; this was a harassment statute that I believed he was in violation of,” Cirino said following the ruling, as reported by News 5 Cleveland. “Obviously, he’s free to write on his blog whatever he wants. I just don’t want to be accosted in the Statehouse in the future.”

articles.title: Mike Tyson predicts ‘Trump will win’ midterms
articles.summary: Former professional boxer Mike Tyson popped up at the White House on Friday, briefly speaking to reporters in the West Wing briefing room and pledging support for President Trump. Tyson told reporters he was asked by the White House to travel with Trump to Syracuse, N.Y., for a rally the president is slated to host…
articles.body:
Former professional boxer Mike Tyson popped up at the White House on Friday, briefly speaking to reporters in the West Wing briefing room and pledging support for President Trump.

Tyson told reporters he was asked by the White House to travel with Trump to Syracuse, N.Y., for a rally the president is slated to host there.

The boxer laughed when journalists in the briefing room asked him what he and Trump planned to talk about and prompted a White House staffer to jokingly interject “no tough questions,” as people in the room laughed.

Asked how Republicans would fare in the midterm elections, Tyson responded, “I think Donald Trump will win.”

Trump has been traveling nearly every day to various states around the country to rally support for the GOP, in some cases traveling with notable sports figures like former MLB pitcher Roger Clemens and current members of the Baltimore Ravens.

Tyson and Trump’s friendship goes back years, and crews for an upcoming Netflix documentary about his life reportedly traveled to the White House recently to speak with the president about the boxer’s career and their friendship.

Their history stretches to the 1980s. As a businessman, Trump served as Tyson’s business adviser and later defended the boxer before and after he was convicted of rape in 1992. Trump later appeared among several celebrities at Tyson’s first fight after he was released from prison — against Peter McNeeley in 1995.

The president has sought to attach himself to fighting sports in recent months, holding a primetime UFC fight on the White House lawn this summer.

Tyson appeared at the “Make America Healthy Again” (MAHA) summit in Washington last month on a panel focusing on the “MAHA Athlete,” and he participated in a Super Bowl ad earlier this year promoting the MAHA campaign and urging people to eat “real food.”

articles.title: HHS endorses DEA move to schedule synthetic kratom extracts
articles.summary: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) on Friday added its recommendations to the Drug Enforcement Administration’s (DEA) move to schedule synthetic kratom extracts, putting its support behind the push to regulate the substances colloquially called “gas station opioid.” In July, the DEA announced plans to temporarily schedule a psychoactive compound derived from kratom…
articles.body:
The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) on Friday added its recommendations to the Drug Enforcement Administration’s (DEA) move to schedule synthetic kratom extracts, putting its support behind the push to regulate the substances colloquially called “gas station opioid.”

In July, the DEA announced plans to temporarily schedule a psychoactive compound derived from kratom called 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) and other related compounds as Schedule I, placing it in a category indicating no accepted medical use and a high potential for abuse.

HHS Assistant Secretary for Health Admiral Brian Christine recommended the DEA use concentration- or ratio-based thresholds for determining how to schedule synthetically concentrated kratom extracts.

While 7-OH is naturally present in trace amounts in herbal kratom, a plant originating from Southeast Asia, products synthetically concentrating the compound in high amounts have proliferated, becoming readily available in gas stations or tobacco shops.

The department recommended that 7-OH and mitragynine pseudoindoxyl (MGPI), a related compound, be classified as Schedule I if either compound or a combination of both exceeds “1 milligram per gram in solid powders, encapsulated material, or other solid forms, or exceeds 1 milligram per milliliter in liquid preparations.”

The HHS also recommended this classification if the amount of 7-OH, MGPI or a combination of both in a product makes up more than 1 percent of mitragynine, the primary psychoactive alkaloid in kratom that is much milder than the compounds the DEA and HHS are concerned about.

“Dangerous and addictive opioids do not belong behind convenience store counters,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement. “Our nation’s children and communities deserve protection from harmful substances like 7-OH and other powerful synthetic drugs. The actions taken by the Department of Justice today reflect our commitment to keeping Americans safe and holding drug traffickers accountable.”

HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said: “We listened to the public, followed the science, and developed a clear recommended threshold for temporary scheduling that targets concentrated 7-OH and MGPI without sweeping natural botanical kratom into Schedule I. The Trump Administration will continue taking decisive action against dangerous products that fuel addiction while making sure our policies are grounded in rigorous science.”

articles.title: Zelensky decries US-Russia diesel deal: ‘Gifts to Putin will not bring peace’
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky lambasted President Trump’s Friday deal allowing Russia to supply the U.S. and global market with diesel, arguing the move would give the Kremlin more money to fund its war in Ukraine and undermine peace efforts. “Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world,” Zelensky wrote…
articles.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky lambasted President Trump’s Friday deal allowing Russia to supply the U.S. and global market with diesel, arguing the move would give the Kremlin more money to fund its war in Ukraine and undermine peace efforts.

“Gifts to Putin will not bring peace or any benefit to the civilized world,” Zelensky wrote in a lengthy post on social platform X . “Russia will ‘repay’ the diesel with further terror and perfidy. Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged.”

Following a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Trump announced that Russia would “immediately” supply 300,000 tons of diesel across the globe to mitigate skyrocketing fuel prices tied to both the Ukraine war and the U.S.’s war in Iran.

News of the agreement came as Zelensky’s negotiating team was in Florida for two days of talks with U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on a possible ceasefire, including a proposal to halt attacks on energy infrastructure.

“I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace, another 500,000 Tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 Tons immediately thereafter,” Trump wrote in a Friday afternoon Truth Social post.

The Treasury Department also issued a temporary license easing sanctions on Russian diesel exports.

Zelensky questioned the timing of Trump’s announcement and suggested to reporters that the Ukrainian delegation was being used as a “smokescreen” to cover for the agreement with Russia.

“Our Ukrainian team, our negotiating team, is now in Florida for a two-day visit to hold talks with the American team on ending this terrible war, or at least on securing a ceasefire,” he said in remarks translated into English.

Ukraine’s leader continued, “And at this very moment, while our team is talking with the American team in Florida, at this very moment, the President of the United States is talking with the leader of the Kremlin, the leader of this war, the leader of this aggression.”

The war in Ukraine has waged on for over four years since Russia invaded its westward neighbor in February of 2022. Witkoff and Kushner traveled to Kyiv for the first time in early September to restart peace negotiations between the two countries, which had stalled when the U.S. entered its own military conflict.

Zelensky argued the revenue generated from Russian diesel sales “means more money for this war, more money to inflict suffering on us, without a doubt. “

“It only feeds Putin and gives him the ability to fight even more,” he said, describing the agreement as a “weak decision by strong partners.”

Trump, meanwhile, has floated the deal as a way to bring down fuel costs for American farmers, ranchers and truck drivers as energy proxies climb ahead of next month’s midterm elections.

Diesel prices averaged $6.28 per gallon as of Friday, compared with $3.68 a year earlier, according to AAA .
